material.acceptance_criteria: A CI job starts oscraftd, posts an authorized order over TCP, and observes the ordered unit in GET /delta and a changed state_hash in GET /state within a bounded number of ticks.
material.description: The tick-shed job in .github/workflows/ci.yml posts POST /order over a real socket but asserts only the 200 code and a shed log line. The browser job reads the wasm page, not the server state. No job posts an order and then reads GET /state or GET /delta to see the unit change, so the client-to-server-to-state path is unwitnessed.
material.resolution: TCP order-to-state check: posts /order with the token (200), polls /delta until the unit appears, asserts state hash changed, prints order-state ok unit before after. Caveat: positions are not served, so the line prints hashes, not x,y.
material.subject: No CI job proves a TCP order changes served state end to end
material.witness_plan: New CI job: curl POST /order with the room token, poll GET /delta?since=0 until the player's unit id appears in changed, and assert GET /state state_hash differs from the pre-order value.
